subject: Anthropology
title: Age Sets and Age Grades
description: One-minute skill: Age Sets and Age Grades.

hook.text: Among the Maasai, you're defined not by family name but by the group of men you were initiated with. Age is identity.

buildup.text: Age sets group people initiated together; age grades are the stages they pass through — warrior, elder, and so on.

discovery.text: These systems cut across kinship, creating bonds that unite the whole society and organize labor, warfare, and ritual.

twist.text: Age-based politics challenge Western assumptions. Here, your generation matters more than your family or wealth.

climax.text: Age sets show that political belonging can be organized by time, not territory. Shared experience creates solidarity.

punchline.text: Sometimes your age group is your nation.

quiz.question: What are age sets?
options: Groups of people initiated together who share political identity

details.summary: Age-set systems group people of similar age into named cohorts that progress through life stages together — from warriors to elders. These systems cut across kinship, creating political unity and organizing labor, military service, and governance by age rather than descent.
details.whyItMatters: Age-set systems show that kinship is not the only basis for political organization. By grouping people across families, age-sets create solidarity that transcends kinship-based factionalism, enabling broader political cohesion.
takeaways: Age-sets group same-age cohorts that progress through life stages together
They organize labor, military service, and governance by age
Age-sets cut across kinship, creating cross-family political unity

faq.question: How do age-set systems work in practice?
faq.answer: Among the Maasai, boys of similar age are initiated together into a named age-set. They serve as warriors for roughly fifteen years, then transition to junior elders, then senior elders. Each grade carries specific rights and responsibilities. The system organizes the entire male lifecycle.

faq.question: Do age-set systems apply to women?
faq.answer: In most societies with age-sets, the formal system applies primarily to men. Women may have parallel but less politically prominent age-based groupings. However, women's influence operates through other channels — their relationships to men in different age-sets and their own informal networks.
